title: Purification and cryo-EM structure determination of VCP/p97 dodecamers from mammalian and bacterial cells
protocol: Add 50 μg pCMV-VCP plasmids into 3.7 mL Opti-MEM and mix gently by vortexing at low speed for 5 s at 25°C.
Add 50 μL of 1 mg/mL PEI to the plasmids/Opti-MEM mixture and mix gently by vortexing at low speed for 5 s at 25°C.
Leave the mixture for 5–10 min at 25°C.
Add the PEI/plasmids/Opti-MEM mixture to H1299 cells in the 15 cm culture dishes and mix gently by moving the dishes from front to back and side to side for at least 5 times.
Discard the cell culture medium in the 15 cm culture dishes after 48–72 h post transfection.
Wash cells with 10 mL PBS buffer two times by gently swirling the dishes by hand.
Add 1 mL buffer A into each 15 cm culture dish and incubate on ice for 30 min for cell lysis.
Collect the suspension and centrifuge at 17,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant and add 50 μL Anti-FLAG M2 affinity gel per mL.
Incubate the supernatant-resin mixture at 4°C for 2 hours by gently rotating with a Labquake rotator.
Pellet at 800 g for 1 minute and wash the resin with 1 mL buffer A three times at 4°C.
Add 500 μL FLAG-VCP elution buffer, incubate at 4°C for 1 hour by gently rotating with a Labquake rotator.
Collect the elution supernatant carefully after pelleting the resin.
Repeat step g one more time.
Pause point: Add 1 mL FLAG-VCP elution buffer (with protease inhibitor) and elute after incubation with shaking for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Concentrate the 1 mL elution to 50–100 μL with Amicon Ultra-0.5 Centrifuge Filter Unit with 30 KDa cutoff at 17,000 g for 10 minutes.
Assemble the blue native-PAGE gel electrophoresis unit according to the manufacturer’s manual.
Load 7.5 μL VCP sample mixed with 2.5 μL 4× blue native-PAGE sample buffer.
Perform the gel electrophoresis at 150 V for 90 min at 25°C.
Fix the gel by microwaving in fix solution (40% methanol and 10% acetic acid) on high (950–1,100 watts) for 45 s.
Shake the gel on an orbital shaker for 15 min at 25°C, then decant the fix solution.
Stain the gel with GelCode Blue Stain Reagent by shaking the gel on an orbital shaker for 1 h.
Image the gel using Azure C500 imaging system.
Equilibrate the Superose 6 10/300 GL column using buffer C.
Load 100 μL VCP sample of about 1–2 mg/mL to the column.
Collect all elution fractions starting at 4 mL.
Examine the elution fractions using SDS-PAGE and blue native-PAGE.
Transform pET28a-VCP plasmid into BL21(DE3) cells using the 42°C heat shock method.
Mix 1 μL of prepared pET28a-VCP plasmid (20 ng/μL) with 50 μL freshly thawed chemically competent BL21(DE3) cells and incubate on ice for 30–45 minutes.
Transfer the tube to a 42°C water or metal bath for 45 seconds and then quickly cool down by putting on ice for 3 minutes.
Add 200 μL LB medium to the tube and shake at 200 rpm, 37°C for 1 hour.
Spread 50 μL of culture on a LB agar plate containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Incubate for 16–24 hours at 37°C.
Pick a single colony and inoculate 5 mL LB supplemented with 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Culture the inoculated medium at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm for 16–24 hours.
Transfer the culture to 400 mL LB (50 μg/mL kanamycin) and incubate until OD600 reaches 0.4–0.6.
Adjust the temperature to 20°C and add 0.4 mM IPTG to induce protein expression for 18 hours.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,000 g for 10 minutes to harvest them.
Resuspend ∼2-3 grams of cells in 20 mL His-VCP lysis buffer with protease inhibitor (1 mM PMSF).
Lysate the cells by sonication (35% power, 1 second on and 3 seconds off for a total of 3 minutes) on ice.
Centrifuge the lysed mixture at 4°C, 17,000 g for 30 minutes to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to a 50 mL tube and add 1 mL 50% Ni-NTA agarose (prewashed with His-VCP lysis buffer).
Incubate and mix gently by rotating at 4°C for 1 hour.
Transfer the mixture to a 15 mL chromatography gravity column.
Wash the resin with 30 mL His-VCP lysis buffer supplemented with 20 mM imidazole at 4°C.
Repeat washing with 20 mL His-VCP lysis buffer supplemented with 40 mM imidazole at 4°C.
Elute bound His-VCP using 5 mL His-VCP elution buffer (containing 500 mM imidazole).
Repeat the elution step one more time.
Pause and incubate with His-VCP elution buffer for 5 min if necessary.
Concentrate the elution using Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifuge Filter Unit with 30 KDa cutoff to about 1 ml at 1,860 g at 4°C.
Mix the elution by gently pipetting up and down to prevent protein precipitation between centrifuge rounds.
Add 5 ml buffer C and repeat step k.
Repeat steps k and l for 3 more times.
Concentrate the sample to 500 μl.
Measure the protein concentration using nanodrop.
Prepare 50 μl aliquots and flash freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Store at -80°C until use.
Dilute His-VCP to 1–2 mg/ml using buffer C.
Add 0.5 U/mg apyrase to treat His-VCP at 25°C for 12–18 h.
Increase apyrase concentration to double if necessary.
Apply 3.5 μL of purified FLAG-VCP dodecamers or apo bacterial recombinant His-VCP to the GO-coated grid.
Blot the grid for 6–9 seconds at 20°C with humidity between 70% and 80%.
Plunge-freeze the grid in liquid ethane using a Cp3 cryo plunger (Gatan).
Maintain frozen grids in liquid nitrogen until further use.
Prepare two more frozen grids using optimal conditions for each sample.
Load grids into a high-end cryo-EM microscope such as a 300 KV FEI Titan Krios TEM.
Record projection images with a direct electron detector, such as Gatan K2 Summit.
Collect about 600 and 800 movies for FLAG-VCP and His-VCP, respectively.
Use a frame rate of 5 frames per second and a total dose of about 40 e/Å².
Set the defocus range between −0.8 to −2 μm.
Align frames using MotionCor2 with a dose per frame of 0.96 and B factor of -150.
Use 5 × 5 patches for alignment.
Determine CTF parameters with Gctf using summed micrographs without dose-weighting (binning 2).
Discard micrographs with overall resolutions worse than 6 Å.
Randomly select about 10% of the remaining micrographs.
Perform particle picking using Gautomatch without a template, using a particle diameter of 200 Å.
Select multiple representative classes from step 2D class averages using RELION or cryoSPARC with approximately 10,000 particles (k=30).
Include both top/bottom and side views in the selected classes for template-based particle picking.
Perform a second round of template-based particle picking with Gautomatch.
Import picked particles into cryoSPARC v2 for further image processing.
Process data using an earlier version of cryoSPARC (v2) or newer versions like v3, or use alternative packages such as RELION.
Clean initial particles via 2D classification: For FLAG-VCP, retain about 40,000 particles from an initial set of 60,000.
For apo His-VCP, retain about 71,600 particles after cleaning from an initial set of 100,000.
Build 3 initial models using the ab initio model module in cryoSPARC with default settings.
Perform hetero-refinements using the 3 models with an initial low pass filtering of 60 Å.
Identify a best class of 27,500 dodecamer particles and two other classes of dodecamer or hexamer particles (8,800 and 3,800 particles) for FLAG-VCP.
For apyrase-treated His-VCP, identify a hexamer class of about 38,300 particles and a dodecamer class of about 33,300 particles.
Repeat the hetero-refinement step to improve the homogeneity of individual classes when necessary.
Perform homo-refinements using default settings of cryoSPARC with D7 symmetry imposition.
Sharpen the maps using phenix.autosharpen according to the resolutions of the maps.
Fit the ATPγS-bound VCP structure into the density map as a rigid body in Chimera.
Segment the density for a single subunit using the “color zone” routine in Chimera.
Carry out manual adjustment and real-space refinement of the atomic model against the subunit density in COOT.
Perform real space refinement in PHENIX using phenix.real_space_refine.
Repeat steps 31 and 32 until good fitting of the atomic model with the density.
Generate oligomer models using phenix.map_symmetry with input density map and resolution.
Use phenix.apply_ncs with the refined single subunit model from previous step.
Refine the oligomer model against the whole density map using Coot.
Refine the oligomer model further using phenix.real_space_refine with settings used in steps 31–33.
Analyze quality of final models with MolProbity in Phenix.
Generate refinement statistics.
